Commentary.Commentary: UPDATE 1505 local (0205 GMT) - Yes! We have the news. Play to begin at 1520 local. Just around 15 minutes from now.

UPDATE 1500 local (0200 GMT) - The rain seems to have stopped. The covers are being removed. Blue skies out of nowhere at the moment. The umpires are strolling out in the middle, inspecting the conditons. It shouldn't take long for the resumption of West Indies' second innings.

Right! West Indies still trail by 381 runs. They will be batting again as Williamson has enforced the follow on. There's plenty of overs left in the day and the Kiwis will look to repeat what they have done so far in the day. Also, just to update, as soon as the Windies innings ended, it started to drizzle heavily and the covers were quickly brought on to protect the 22-yard strip. We will keep you posted.

Windies batters just had no answers to the Southee masterclass who got good support from the others to wrap this innings up quickly. After getting no success in 26 overs last evening, the Kiwi bowlers decided to do the magic on Day 3. Southee struck in his first over and gave the team a perfect start. It was all about their swing bowlers after that. They got some sort of resistance only from Blackwood and Holder. Southee eventually ended up with a 4-fer while Wagner and Jamieson got two. Boult got just one to his name.

The West Indies openers were able to weather the storm last evening and they probably needed to do something similar in the first hour but they failed to do so. The others who followed couldn't do much either and they were soon left reeling with the side gone with the score not crossing 100. Skipper Holder and Blackwood then added 40 runs between them to offer some resistance. However, Blackwood fell in the 4th over of the second session. Holder stayed till the end but lost partners from the other end.

Right! Dowrich will not bat which means it is the end of the West Indies' innings. A sorry batting show from the Windies batters here in this innings and the bad news for them is that Kane Williamson has enforced the follow on.

OUT! LBW! Umpire's call on hitting the wicket. Wagner gets his second wicket. After bowling a bumper he goes for the fuller one to Gabriel. He looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pad. An appeal and the finger is raised. Gabriel refers it upstairs but it won't help as there is no bat which is confirmed by the Ultra Edge. And the Ball Tracker shows that it will be umpire's call on hitting the wicket.
Review time! Wagner has got his man? The umpire thinks so but Gabriel signals the 'T'. That looked plumb. Let's see what the replays have to say.

UPDATE 1344 local (0044 GMT) - Good news! The covers are coming off. We are not too far away from the resumption. It will start at 1350 local.

UPDATE 1337 local (0037 GMT) - We were just minutes away from the 2nd session on Day 3 but it has started to drizzle. The groundsmen quickly brings the covers on to protect the pitch. Let's hope this goes away quickly.

It was Southee who took the ball first up and struck in the first over itself as he removed Campbell. Brooks became his 2nd victim in the next over and Boult said I should join the party too. He got rid of Brathwaite and West Indies were in all sorts of trouble. Bravo and Chase then weathered the storm for a while but eventually fell to Jamieson and Wagner respectively. Holder, the Windies skipper, was dismissed for nothing but Wagner overstepped and gave him life. He along with Blackwood have now added 35 runs but the task for them is much bigger. Will they be able to continue the fight when we return for the second session of this moving day? We will soon find out. Join us in a bit.

We are all set to begin Day 3. The New Zealand players are out in the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell will resume their innings for West Indies. Tim Southee will start the proceedings for Day 3.

Hello and welcome to Day 3! The Kiwis put on a massive score the other day, courtesy, a brilliant double ton from skipper Kane Williamson. It is now up to the bowlers to do the job. They bowled 26 overs on Day 2 but Brathwaite and Campbell did well to negotiate that phase. A new day will bring new challenges for both sides. Will the Kiwis be able to strike or will the Windies openers be able to continue their stand from the last evening? We will know all these in a short while when the action resumes.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Right! 49-run unbeaten opening stand! On Day 3, when these two will come out to bat, the target for them will be to bat as long as they could. West Indies bat long and would hope that all their batters do well and take the game deep. The hosts, on the other hand, would return on Day 3 and look to get rid of this stand first and then go about their business. Day 2 belongs to the Kiwis but the way these two are batting, the New Zealand bowlers might have to do the toil if they are to take the honors for the 3rd day as well. So, when we return for Day 3, it is going to be another intriguing day's play! Do join us for the same. Until then, it is goodbye from our side. Take care!

Then came the Windies openers! They were tested by Southee and Boult in the first few overs but they weathered the storm. Jamieson too bowled well but couldn't produce the magic delivery. Wagner arrived and started bowling the bouncers but Campbell and Brathwaite did well to negotiate him as well.

Nothing much to talk about the Windies bowling. They weren't bad but just couldn't find the way to get the big wicket of Williamson. Gabriel struck early, Roach removed Nicholls but after that, it was hard work for the bowlers. Roach had managed to get the wicket of Williamson but he overstepped and gave Kane another chance. It was Joseph who eventually got the wicket of Williamson but not before the Kiwi skipper got to his first-ever 250 in Tests. Declaration eventually came and that would've given a sigh of relief to the Windies bowlers who had to toil really hard in the course of these 2 days, bowling 145 overs.

It was all about Kane Williamson! The day started with New Zealand losing Ross Taylor early. Nicholls didn't last long too but Kane continued as he got good support from the likes of Blundell, Mitchell, and Jamieson. He went past 250 and got out trying to up the ante. Jamieson got to his maiden half ton and the Kiwis declared after that.
Fine phase of play for West Indies! Their openers have managed to remain unscathed! But the day will belong to the Kiwis and especially to their skipper Kane Williamson for his classy knock of 251.

Drinks! Good phase of play for West Indies. The openers have done well to see off the initial danger. The ball has beaten the outside edge a few times but Brathwaite and Campbell have done well. They will look to continue doing the same and end the day unscathed. New Zealand will want to have at least one wicket to their name.
Back of a length on off, Brathwaite keeps it out.
Good length delivery on middle, Brathwaite keeps it out.

Four? Well, we thought so and so did the commentators on air. Brathwaite had slammed it off the meat of the bat and it was heading to the fence. But, but. The backward point had other things on his mind. He dived to his left and makes an excellent stop.
Full delivery on off, Brathwaite pushes it to mid off.
Gets behind this time and blocks it.
That was a beauty! Good length and around off, Brathwait looks to defend but misses.
Leave to end the over as Southee bowls this one outside off again.
Gets closer to around off and bangs it short. Campbell drops his wrists and lets it go to the keeper.
Outside off again, Campbell allows it to go to the keeper.
Another leave as this one is bowled outside off.
In the channel outside off, John shoulders arms.
Good length and around off, Campbell defends it.
Change of ends for Southee.
A couple of runs to end Jamieson's over. Shortish and on middle, Brathwaite tucks it wide of the fine leg fielder. Before he can come around, two taken.
On middle, this one is tucked towards the leg side.

Just a hint of shape away and the bat is beaten again. Or maybe not. This one is fuller and just outside off, Brathwaite looks to play at it but looks like he pulled away his bat again, at the very last moment.
Outside off, left alone.
Gets to move it away again. This time it is just outside off, Kraigg thinks of playing at it but at the last moment pulls it out from doing that.
Nice start for him. Pitches this around off and goes away a touch. Brathwaite does well to defend it with soft hands.
Here's Kyle Jamieson with the ball. A half ton with the bat earlier in the day. Can he provide the breakthrough?
Another delivery on the pads, this time Brathwaite works it towards fine leg and keeps the strike for the next over.
On the leg stump line, tucked towards square leg for an easy run.
Goes for the bouncer again but this time misses his line. This one is down the leg side. Campbell lets it be.
Ouch! Sharp bouncer from Boult. It is just outside off. Campbell is late in getting out of the way. The ball hits him on the chest.
In the channel outside off, this time Campbell lets it be.
Beaten! Good length and just outside off, Campbell looks to defend but misses.
Length ball around off, Brathwaite defends it towards cover. 7 off the over.
Fuller and on the pads, Campbell nudges it towards square leg and takes a run.
Good length but little too wide outside off for Campbell to play at it.
FOUR! SHOT! Fine shot. First boundary of the Windies innings. Full and wide outside off, Campbell creams it through the cover region and it races away to the fence
Around off on a length, blocked.
Full and on the pads from Boult now. Campbell flicks it through mid-wicket and gets two.
On the pads again, Campbell clips it towards square leg and takes a single to keep the strike for the next over.
Fuller and on the pads, Campbell looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pad.
Full on middle, Campbell drives it to mid on.

Short ball but down the leg side. Brathwaite has nothing to do with it.

Campbell is not happy with his bat. The new willow is out for him.
Length ball on middle, Campell blocks it off his back foot. Maiden from Trent.
Outside off, left alone.
Good leave! Just outside off on a good length, Campbell covers his timber and shoulders arms.
Goes a tad fuller and bowls it outside off, Campbell lets it be.

Lovely delivery. Boult runs in and bowls it just behind good length. It pitches around off and then a touch of away movement is all it needs to beat the outside edge. Boult is not too far away from getting that outside edge it seems.
Back of a length and around off, Campbell defends it out.
Full and on middle, Brathwaite pushes it to mid on.
Little wide outside off, Brathwaite has nothing to do with it.
Fullish and around off, Brathwaite is solid in defense.

Appeal for a catch but not out says the umpire. Full ball down the leg side, Brathwaite looks to flick but misses. The keeper takes the catch and they appeal but not out says the umpire. There was a noise but it came off the pad.
Campbell is up and running. Fuller and on the pads, he flicks it to deep square leg to open his account.
Good leave! Very good leave! It is pitched around middle and off, it goes away just a touch but Campbell covers his sticks and leaves the ball on length.
Ripper to end the over! Squared the batsman there did Boult. Just behind good length and around off, Brathwaite pokes at it with hard hands but the ball shapes away to beat the outside edge.
Good length and around middle, worked past the short leg fielder. It was uppish but went past the fielder really fast.
Around off on a length, blocked off the back foot.
Beauty from Boult! Pitches this just around off and makes it go away. Brathwaite pokes at it but is beaten.
Good length delivery on middle, Brathwaite defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery on off, Brathwaite punches it to covers.
WIDE! Boult starts with a bouncer, Brathwaite ducks under it.
Who will partner with Southee from the other end? It is Trent Boult.
Fullish and around off for the left-hander from Southee. Campbell comes on the front foot and pushes it back to the bowler.
Pokes this one through backward point and gets to the other end.
Southee goes full and outside off, asking Brathwaite to go for the expansive drive but the West Indies openers stays back to defend it.
In the channel outside off, Brathwaite lets it be.
Brathwaite is off the mark! A shortish ball on middle and leg, he works it towards deep square leg and scampers back for the second.

We are back for the second innings. The New Zealand players are out in the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell will open the innings for West Indies. Tim Southee will start the proceedings for New Zealand.
Southee is on the money straightaway! A length ball just outside off, moves a touch away as Brathwaite looks to defend but gets beaten.
